exemplars.title: Investigating Semantically-enhanced Exploration of GAN Latent Space via a Digital Mood Board
exemplars.why: The interaction nearly reproduces the structural signature step by step: the user separately selects two existing groups, invokes a named Mix operation for each, and receives a synthesized style mixture between the identifiable operands.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: Chosen above VoiceForge because its evidence explicitly distinguishes operand selection from operator invocation and documents the complete interaction sequence.

exemplars.title: VoiceForge: A Text-Driven Character Voice Generation System for Narrative Content Creation
exemplars.why: Users choose one to three existing audio references and fuse them through a visible mixing panel whose adjustable weights expose continuous movement among the operands, making the system's interpolative contribution directly controllable.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: Chosen above DanceGen because adjustable per-reference weights make the combination mechanism visible and rebuildable, whereas DanceGen's evidence does not describe how its blend is controlled.

exemplars.title: DanceGen: Supporting Choreography Ideation and Prototyping with Generative AI
exemplars.why: The gallery establishes retained dance sequences as existing operands, after which users select multiple sequences and apply blending to synthesize another sequence in the same choreographic space.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: Chosen above the fashion style-mixing panel because DanceGen more clearly treats complete, retained artifacts as operands, while the alternative describes selecting elements and leaves the resulting fused artifact unstated.

notes: I retained the consensus top three but reversed the first two: rid 7000 ranks first because its quote most explicitly proves the signature's separate selection and invocation acts. No score was adjusted by more than 0.3. The main evidentiary weakness is that none of the three quotes confirms that a fused result can itself become a later operand. VoiceForge also leaves the generated same-space result implicit, while DanceGen does not document its blend control or output presentation.
